text: The Song—best of all songs—Solomon's song!
Yes! For your love is better than wine,
The syllables of your name murmur like a meadow brook. No wonder everyone loves to say your name!
An elopement with my King-Lover! We'll celebrate, we'll sing, we'll make great music. Yes! For your love is better than vintage wine. Everyone loves you—of course! And why not?
oh, dear sisters in Jerusalem, Weather-darkened like Kedar desert tents, time-softened like Solomon's Temple hangings.
darkened by the sun's harsh rays. My brothers ridiculed me and sent me to work in the fields. They made me care for the face of the earth, but I had no time to care for my own face.
—I love you so much— Tell me where you're tending your flocks, where you let them rest at noontime. Why should I be the one left out, outside the orbit of your tender care?
it's all right. Stay with your flocks. Lead your lambs to good pasture. Stay with your shepherd neighbors.
strands of jewels illumine the curve of your throat.
that will mark and accent your beauty.
the head of my lover was a sachet of sweet myrrh.
picked just for me from the fields of Engedi.
And your eyes so beautiful—like doves!
And the bed we share is like a forest glen.
enclosed by cypresses, fragrant and green.
